note: A hand-labelled sample of employers' job postings, for tests/unit/postings-read.unit.ts. 480 postings drawn on 2026-11-19 from 26 employers' public boards: half whose title a naive word match would keep, half it would refuse; split in two, `tune` (the reader was built against it) and `held` (it was not looked at until the reader was done). Each keeps its title, department, location and a few lines of its text (`lines`), not the posting. `career` lists the careers a careful reader accepts, the right one first, null where refusing is right or accepted; `level` the accepted level words; `places` the US places (`placesOptional`: the field does not give the state, so none is accepted too). 100 of the kept ones carry `asks`: the skills and makes its lines ask for (`any`: one of these counts; `optional`: may be found or not), its requirements and pay as stated in those lines (a value that starts with "?" is not counted). 20 more were added on 2026-11-26 (`added`; n 480 to 499, all in `tune`, with no `naive`): titles of cleaning and food preparation work, which left the catalogue that day and which the reader must turn away. Three are titles as production's board had them (Sanitation Technician I and Sanitation Specialist I at Cargill, a grocery store's Meat Cutter at H-E-B); the rest are the names such jobs go by. Their `lines` were written by hand, not drawn from a posting: what such a posting asks for, in the catalogue's own words where it has them, so the title is turned away whatever the text names. 24 more were added the same day (`added`; n 500 to 523, all in `tune`, with no `naive`) for the words that make a title not ours (data/careers/aliases.json, `notOurs`): 20 titles that hold one of the words beside a career's own name ("Janitorial Maintenance Technician", "General Laborer - Sanitation"), one or more for each word, which the reader must turn away though their lines name that career's skills; and four titles of factory work that hold a word left off the list on purpose (facilities, building, cleanroom, a foundry's cleaning room), which it must keep. All 24 are names such jobs go by, at made-up employers, and their `lines` were written by hand. The production welder, the same day: a production welder is the MIG Welder, not the several-process Welder (data/careers/aliases.json: "production welder" is another name of MIG Welder; the owner's question of that day). The two "Production Welder" postings the sample already held (n 49 in `held`, n 148 in `tune`, both John Deere's) were labelled Welder when they were drawn and are labelled MIG Welder now (`relabelled`): the only labels ever changed, and nothing else of either. Four more were added (`added`; n 524 to 527, in `tune`, with no `naive`): the other "Production Welder" titles of John Deere's board as production had them, each with its department and location as the board gave them, each a MIG Welder. Their `lines` were written by hand from what each posting was read to ask for (forklifts in all four, MIG and robotic welding in one); no text of a posting is kept.
